etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Ancient Greek πνευμονία (pneumonía, “lung disease”), from πνεύμων (pneúmōn, “lung”) + -ία (-ía).

definitions.definition: An acute or chronic inflammation of the lungs caused by viruses, bacteria or other microorganisms, or sometimes by physical or chemical irritants.

quote.citation: 1922, Michael Arlen, “2/9/1”, in “Piracy”: A Romantic Chronicle of These Days‎[1]:
quote.text: He had always been remarkably immune from such little ailments, and had only once in his life been ill, of a vicious pneumonia long ago at school.
